pois.name: Roppongi Hills
pois.description: A revolutionary mixed-use development (2003) by Mori Building — 54-storey tower, 200+ shops, 21 restaurants, cinemas, and the Mori Art Museum on the 53rd floor. The 45m 'Mori Garden' preserves the historic Akasaka Moto-Kiyozumi mansion grounds. A city-within-a-city that redefined Tokyo's urban planning.

pois.name: Mori Art Museum
pois.description: Tokyo's premier contemporary art museum, located on the 53rd floor of Roppongi Hills. The 'Mori Building Digital Art Museum' collaboration with teamLab has drawn over 10 million visitors. The museum's mission is to bring contemporary art to a mass audience — no permanent collection, only boundary-pushing temporary exhibitions.

pois.name: Tokyo Tower Observatory
pois.description: The iconic 333m communications tower (1958) — Tokyo's answer to the Eiffel Tower, but 13m taller. The Main Deck (150m) and Top Deck (250m) offer panoramic views. Illuminated in orange (standard) or gold (special occasions), it's the defining silhouette of Tokyo's skyline.

pois.name: Roppongi Nightlife District
pois.description: Tokyo's most international nightlife district — bars, clubs, and restaurants catering to expats and tourists. The 'Roppongi Crossing' area around the intersection is the epicentre, with everything from tiny izakaya to superclubs. The area has gentrified significantly since the 2000s, shedding its seedy reputation.

pois.name: 21_21 Design Sight
pois.description: A design museum founded by Issey Miyake and Tadao Ando (2007). The concrete structure with its 16m glass atrium is itself a masterpiece. Exhibitions focus on industrial design, architecture, and everyday objects — the 2023 'Design for the Future' show drew 500,000 visitors.
